MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Analysis

PATIENT: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
AGE/SEX: 73-year-old male
ORDERING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Diagnosis: Newly diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma
Reason for testing: Molecular characterization for targeted therapy selection

SPECIMEN
Type: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue
Site: Lung
Block ID: [redacted ID]

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for:
- ALK (2p23) rearrangement
- ROS1 (6q22) rearrangement

METHODOLOGY
FISH analysis was performed on 4-micron tissue sections using the following probes:
- ALK: Vysis ALK Break Apart FISH Probe Kit (Abbott Molecular)
- ROS1: Vysis ROS1 Break Apart FISH Probe Kit (Abbott Molecular)

Procedure: Tissue sections were deparaffinized, pretreated, and hybridized with fluorescent probes according to manufacturer's protocols. Signal patterns were evaluated using fluorescence microscopy.

RESULTS

ALK FISH: ANALYSIS INCOMPLETE - INSUFFICIENT TUMOR CELLS
ROS1 FISH: ANALYSIS INCOMPLETE - INSUFFICIENT TUMOR CELLS

The tissue sections submitted for analysis contained insufficient viable tumor cells for reliable FISH interpretation. Multiple areas were examined, but adequate tumor cell density could not be achieved for either ALK or ROS1 testing. A minimum of 50 tumor cells is required for accurate assessment.

INTERPRETATION
Molecular characterization for ALK and ROS1 rearrangements could not be completed due to insufficient tumor cellularity in the submitted specimen. These analyses are critical for identifying patients who may benefit from targeted therapy with ALK or ROS1 inhibitors.

RECOMMENDATIONS
A new tissue biopsy with adequate tumor content is recommended for completion of ALK and ROS1 FISH testing. Alternative testing methods such as next-generation sequencing (NGS) on a new specimen may also be considered for comprehensive molecular profiling.
